 CNW Group Fri, October 30, 2026 at 6:01 AM MDT 4 min read CL=F +1.96% 
 ^GSPC -0.30% 
 TORONTO, Oct. 30, 2026 /CNW/ -- Canadian defined benefit (DB) pension plans in RBC Investor Services' custody posted a median return of -2.6% in the third quarter of 2026 and 4.5% year-to-date, reversing a 6.0% gain in the second quarter. The same rise in bond yields that drove fixed income losses may also have improved plan funded status by lowering the value of future liabilities. The quarter unfolded against a backdrop of geopolitical uncertainty, with Middle East tensions driving sharp swings in oil prices throughout the quarter. 
 RBC Equities hold the line as energy leads 
Client plans returned 1.2% in global equities in Q3 2026, versus the MSCI World Index (CAD) at 1.9%. Within the global equity universe, U.S. equities led the way, with the S&P 500 Index (CAD) returning 2.4%. Energy was the standout sector in the S&P 500 Index at 17.3%, supported by elevated oil prices. Information technology, the largest allocation in the S&P 500 Index at 39.7% of the benchmark, returned 7.3%, building on Q2 gains. Only two other sectors posted positive returns; the remaining seven were negative. Regionally, European equities lagged, with the MSCI Europe Index (CAD) returning -1.6% for the quarter. 
 Client plans returned 1.6% in Canadian equities, broadly tracking the TSX Composite Index return. Financials, the index's largest allocation at 34.4%, declined 3.0%, but three positive sectors offset negative returns across the remaining eight. Information Technology was the top-performing sector at 17.9%, followed by Materials at 12.9%, benefiting from the safe-haven appeal of precious metals. Energy posted modest gains of 3.3% and ranked as the top sector on a year-to-date basis at 27.7%. 
 Fixed income under pressure as interest rates climb 
Client plans returned -5.1% in fixed income, versus the FTSE Canada Universe Bond Index at -3.0%. Fixed income posted negative returns across nearly all segments. Only the 91-day Treasury bill (0.6%) and mortgage bonds (1.5%) posted positive returns for the quarter. Long-term saw the steepest decline, with the FTSE Canada Long Overall Index declining 6.3%, while short-term bonds returned -0.9%. The Government of Canada 10-year bond yield rose 61 basis points over the quarter. For pension plans, that rise in yields may have improved funded status by lowering the value of future liabilities, though the extent depends on each plan's liability profile. 
 Plan sponsors seek deeper portfolio transparency 
Asset owners are increasingly focused on understanding their total portfolio risk, moving beyond traditional asset class allocations to examine specific thematic concentrations. Private markets are a particular area of focus, as they can present limited visibility into underlying exposures. Smaller and mid-size plans are driving increased demand for transparency and disclosure from investment managers. 
 Story Continues "A quarter like this one shows why headline returns can be misleading. Plan sponsors saw negative performance, but rising yields may have actually strengthened their funded position. That disconnect is driving a real shift in how they think about their portfolios," said Isabelle Tremblay, Director, Client Solutions, and Asset Owner Segment Lead, RBC Investor Services. 
 Bank of Canada holds through Q3 before raising rates in Q4 
The Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% through both rate announcements during the quarter, as upside risks to inflation from elevated energy prices and new tariffs were weighed against increasingly uncertain growth prospects. At its October 28 meeting, held after the close of the quarter, the Bank raised the policy rate to 2.5%.
